tax.text: Allen supports a wealth tax and restoring the corporate tax rate after its 2017 cut.
tax.quote: Allen: endorses Warren’s two-cent-on-the-dollar wealth tax framework; supports raising the corporate rate from its 2017 cut; draws on her city council work reviewing tax abatements and says we should only reward businesses that offer living wages

wages.text: Allen supports an inflation-indexed national minimum wage and protecting workers' right to unionize.
wages.quote: Ensuring your paycheck covers your basic needs through a national minimum wage tied to inflation.

trade.text: Allen proposes removing tariffs from food and other essential goods.
trade.quote: Making your groceries more affordable by removing tariffs on food and other essentials and stopping corporate price hikes.

debt.text: Allen rules out raising the Social Security retirement age and supports lifting the payroll-tax cap to sustain the program.
debt.quote: Allen: calls it non-negotiable; rules out raising the retirement age; supports lifting the payroll cap and taxing wealthy investment income more aggressively

housing.text: Allen supports investing in additional homes for working families and expanding affordable-housing programs.
housing.quote: Making homeownership more affordable through investments that build homes for working families, not luxury condos.

schools.text: Allen calls for full funding of public schools and continued federal support through the Department of Education.
schools.quote: Full funding for our schools so that all students can receive a high-quality education.

immigration.text: Allen supports pathways to legal entry and citizenship, keeping families together and protecting due process.
immigration.quote: Prioritizing immigration reform that is smart and humane, protecting current residents while providing pathways to entry and citizenship for those seeking to become Americans.

guns.text: Allen answered yes when asked whether she supports a federal assault-weapons ban.
guns.quote: Federal assault weapons ban: Rector — Yes / Zeigler — Yes / Allen — Yes

cannabis.text: Allen answered yes when asked whether recreational cannabis should be legalized federally.
cannabis.quote: Federal legalization of recreational cannabis: Rector — Yes / Zeigler — Yes / Allen — Yes

health.text: Allen supports preserving ACA subsidies while moving toward Medicare for All or a single-payer system.
health.quote: Allen: supports a transitional approach — ACA subsidies as a near-term Band-Aid, moving toward Medicare for all or a single-payer system

energy.text: Allen supports stricter pollution enforcement and investment in wind, solar and modern electric-grid infrastructure while also emphasizing lower energy costs.
energy.quote: Lower energy costs, diversify our energy supply, and create thousands of local, clean-energy jobs by investing in wind, solar, and modern grid infrastructure.

voting.text: Allen opposed the SAVE Act as an unnecessary attempt to restrict voter access.
voting.quote: We're making up a problem or a solution to a problem that doesn’t exist.

tax.text: Messmer supported the One Big Beautiful Bill and called for additional tax cuts for families and businesses.
tax.quote: The One Big Beautiful Bill prevented the largest tax increase in history from crushing hard-working Americans, while making many pro-growth tax policies permanent for all families and businesses

wages.text: Messmer joined a congressional letter seeking to freeze the federally required wage for H-2A agricultural workers at its January 2023 level.
wages.quote: we request that the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations bill prohibit funds from being used to implement a wage larger than the January 2023 wage rate or otherwise freeze the H-2A wage rates at January 2023 levels

trade.text: Messmer said long-term tariffs and resulting retaliation could harm agriculture and the broader economy, while allowing that tariffs might be useful temporarily in negotiations.
trade.quote: I don’t know that long-term tariffs are going to be helpful with the retaliatory tariffs

schools.text: Messmer supported an Indiana budget that increased K-12 funding while expanding school-choice programs.
schools.quote: At nearly half of the overall budget, K-12 funding received a historic $2.9 billion increase over the next two years while expanding school choice for families.

safety.text: Messmer praised deploying National Guard troops to assist local police with crime enforcement in Washington, D.C.
safety.quote: These dedicated public servants are helping to return law and order to a place where the crime crisis had become uncontrollable.

guns.text: Messmer co-sponsored and defended an Indiana law prohibiting the tracking of firearm purchases through merchant-category codes.
guns.quote: Hoosiers have a constitutional right to bear arms, and I believe House Enrolled Act 1084 will help uphold that right.

abortion.text: Messmer said he opposes abortion in most cases and introduced legislation penalizing the nonconsensual administration of abortion-inducing drugs.
abortion.quote: I am against abortion in most cases, but it is unconscionable to even consider tricking a woman into killing her unborn baby

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: Messmer cosponsored legislation defining sex biologically and barring males from female amateur athletic competitions.
gender.quote: Arizona, Mr. Messmer, Mr. Bost, Mr. Van Orden, Mr. Carter of Texas, Mr. Timmons, and Mr. Gosar) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on the Judiciary

cannabis.text: Messmer expressed reservations about full legalization while remaining open to regulated medical marijuana and reduced penalties for small-scale possession.
cannabis.quote: Fully legalizing marijuana is going to be difficult at the state level as long as the federal government considers it a Class 1 controlled substance. I would be open to listening to the debate on regulated medical marijuana use.

health.text: Messmer advocated allowing insurance purchases across state lines to increase competition and the number of carriers.
health.quote: Why not change the rules that would allow me to buy insurance across State lines to bring more competition and more carriers into our markets?

energy.text: Messmer supported keeping Indiana coal plants operating to preserve grid reliability, coal jobs and lower electricity costs.
energy.quote: Continued coal production will protect the energy grid and prevent electricity blackouts, while also providing lower energy costs, especially during extreme weather conditions.

voting.text: Messmer supported federal photo-identification, citizenship-verification and voter-roll-check requirements.
voting.quote: Strengthening voter ID and citizenship verification standards through the SAVE America Act will protect the integrity of future federal elections.
